==When to use==
This template indicates that the article [[Wikipedia:Citing sources|cites]] a sufficient number of [[Wikipedia:Reliable sources|reliable sources]], but uses an ''inappropriate'' combination of inline citations and [[WP:Citing sources#General_reference|general references]]. All material in articles must be [[WP:Verifiability|verifiable]], but outside of [[WP:Featured articles|featured articles]] and [[WP:Good article criteria|good articles]] Wikipedia does not require the use of inline citations except to support [[direct quotations]], material that has been challenged or is likely to be challenged and contentious material about [[Wikipedia:Biographies of living persons|living persons]].

An [[WP:INCITE|inline citation]] is ''any'' system that associates a given piece of an article with a specific citation. Do not add this tag to articles that use the "wrong" style of inline citation.

For articles that do not contain any general references, but that need a greater number of citations, use {{tl|More citations needed}} instead.

== How to use ==

To add this template to an article, copy and paste:
* {{tlx|{{PAGENAME}}|<nowiki>{{subst:DATE}}</nowiki>}}
:or
* {{tlx|{{PAGENAME}}|date{{=}}{{CURRENTMONTHNAME}} {{CURRENTYEAR}}}}

Both options result in the same output.

The template can be placed in the article's "References" section, or, as appropriate for the citation style, "Notes" section.

An optional unnamed parameter:
*{{tlx|{{PAGENAME}}|section|date{{=}}{{CURRENTMONTHNAME}} {{CURRENTYEAR}}}}
will change the word "article" in "This article...", e.g. <code>{{tlx|{{PAGENAME}}|list}}</code> or {{tlx|{{PAGENAME}}|table}}.  When used this way, the template cannot be placed in the "References" section.

This template will add the article to [[:Category:Articles lacking in-text citations]].

The template also has an optional {{para|BLP}} parameter. If its value is <var>yes</var>, this will indicate that the article is a [[WP:Biographies of living persons |biography of a living person]], which have higher standards for further reading and external links.

You can add {{para|small|yes}} to make the template smaller and left-justified. This form factor is primarily used with {{para||section}} and when the template is put in the References section (typically after {{tlx|Reflist}} and before a pile of "general references" that are not cited inline in the article).

To change the output "largely unverified" to "partially unverified", use the parameter {{para|partial|yes}} or {{para|partial|y}}.  This is appropriate for article that do have a significant number of inline citations but which also have a pile of references that have not been cited inline.  (Do not confuse this with articles that in one section of references use short inline citations to the same works more fully specified in a second references section.)

The following parameter is obsolete and deprecated: {{para|{{strongbad|suffix}}}} (simply use the first unnamed parameter).

==Examples==

{{demo|<nowiki>{{More footnotes needed|section|date=February 2011}}</nowiki>}}
<br />
{{demo|<nowiki>{{More footnotes needed|BLP=yes|date=February 2011}}</nowiki>}}
